title: Top-degree derived base change on global Leray classes in a commutative square
statement: Let f:X\to S, q:Y\to T, g:T\to S and p:Y\to X be scheme morphisms with pf=qg [def-pc-scheme]. Let F and M be module sheaves on X and Y and let a:p^*F\to M [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-module-pullback]. Put C=Rf_*(F[0]) and assume H^i(C)=0 for i>1 [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Let d:Lg^*C\to Rq_*(M[0]) be the single-degree base-change composite followed by Rq_*(a[0]) [def-weil-pbc-single-degree-module-base-change-composite]. Let κ:H^1(Lg^*C)\xrightarrow{\sim}g^*H^1(C) be the specified top comparison [lem-weil-pbc-derived-pullback-top-cohomology]. Let ε_f and ε_q be the cocycle Leray edges [lem-pc-leray-degenerate-sections], transported to total-derived cohomology by the canonical total/classical comparison. Let s_g be global section pullback induced by the normalized tensor adjunction unit, identifying g^{-1}(S)=T [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. For every x\in H^1(X,F), one has ε_q(p_a^*x)=Γ(T,H^1(d)κ^{-1})(s_g(ε_f(x))). Here p_a^* is precisely the module-cohomology map for the ordinary adjunct of a [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. No cartesian, affine, flatness or invertibility hypothesis on d is imposed.

proof.text: Uniqueness of the section-normalized tensor adjunction identifies it with the adjunction chosen in exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction. Apply derivedModuleBaseChange_transpose and naturality in the coefficient map; naturality of the canonical single direct-image comparison identifies the transpose with derivedSquareUnitMap of the ordinary adjunct of a.

The target Rq_*(M[0]) is in D≥0 by the existing single-module right-derived lower-bound theorem. Apply derivedAdjunction_topEdge in degree one to get its local-class edge e and the equality between the ordinary top-cohomology adjunct and H¹ of the derived transpose followed by e.

Apply globalLeray_unitSquare to the ordinary adjunct of a and e. This uses the existing arbitrary-square local class theorem and the single-morphism classical Leray/restricted-resolution identification.

Evaluate the ordinary tensor adjunction at the whole open. Naturality of the coefficient sheaf map across Opens.map_top identifies its section-level adjunct with topDegreeSectionPullback followed by the cohomology map. Combine this with the preceding two equalities.

theorem topDegreeLeray_commutativeSquare
    {X S Y T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (q : Y ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ S) (p : Y ⟶ X)
    (hs : p ≫ f = q ≫ g) (F : X.Modules) (M : Y.Modules)
    (a : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback p).obj F ⟶ M)
    (hC : (topDegreeDerivedImage.{u, w} f F).IsLE 1) :
    let C := topDegreeDerivedImage.{u, w} f F
    let d := topDegreeBaseChangeMap.{u, w} f q g p hs F M a
    let κ := derivedPullbackTopCohomology g 1 C hC
    letI : IsIso κ := (Classical.choose_spec
      (derivedPullback_topCohomology g 1 C hC)).2.1
    ∀ x : topDegreeCohomologyOnBase f F,
      topDegreeLerayEdge q M (topDegreeCohomologyPullback f q p F M a x) =
      (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor T.toRingedSpace).map
        (inv κ ≫ ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor.{w, u, u + 1}
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace)) 1)).map d)
          (topDegreeSectionPullback g (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor.{w, u, u + 1}
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace)) 1)).obj C)
              (topDegreeLerayEdge f F x))
